matmech_techniques: High-Angle Annular Dark-Field Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy (HAADF-STEM)

sub_claims.claim_text: The dense basal planar defects are LPSO nanoplates: aggregates of four-layer Zn/Y-segregated fcc-type stacking faults, not conventional stacking faults

evidence.observation: Bright-field TEM taken with g=0002 shows strong planar fault-like contrast lying on (0001), roughly ten plates per um
HAADF-STEM: the plates appear as bright, heavy-atom-rich bands only a few atomic layers wide; the 1 nm inset resolves one such bright band

sub_claims.claim_text: Twinning and non-basal slip must cut the (0001) LPSO nanoplates, so their CRSS is raised selectively, while basal slip glides parallel to the plates and is left easy

caveats.observation: Basal-slip CRSS is itself raised, from ~0.5 MPa in pure Mg to ~4.3 MPa in the alloy, an ~8x increase

sub_claims.claim_text: Co-add 0.2 at% Zn and 0.6 at% Y to Mg (Mg99.2Zn0.2Y0.6), a dilute composition that contains no perfect LPSO phase
Minute co-addition of Zn and Y, forming LPSO-related nanoplates rather than a perfect LPSO phase, should strongly raise the yield stress of an Mg single crystal
Co-add 0.2 at% Zn and 0.6 at% Y to Mg (Mg99.2Zn0.2Y0.6), a dilute composition that contains no perfect LPSO phase
Yield stress is strongly orientation dependent and, in [11-20] and [01-10], reaches ~145-165 MPa at RT, about 11x the pure-Mg single crystal

evidence.observation: RT yield stress by orientation: ~9 MPa for [1 1 -2 1.85], ~148-165 MPa for [11-20], ~143 MPa for [01-10]; [0001] fractures at ~355 MPa without yielding

Between RT and 400 C the alloy's [11-20]/[01-10] yield stress falls only from ~165 to ~105 MPa, while the gray pure-Mg reference falls from ~270 to ~15 MPa and sits near 10 MPa in the soft orientations
Yield stress in [11-20] at RT: 167 MPa as-grown, 113 MPa after the 520 C anneal, 160 MPa after the further 400 C anneal

evidence.observation: Stress-strain curves: [11-20], [01-10] and [1 1 -2 1.85] all pass 5% plastic strain at RT and 300 C, [0001] fractures without yielding (x at ~355 and ~255 MPa), and only [01-10] at RT work-hardens, 165 -> 205 MPa

matmech_techniques: Scanning Electron Microscopy with Electron Backscatter Diffraction (SEM-EBSD)

sub_claims.claim_text: In tension along [0001] the crystal elongates ~45% at 65-80 MPa by kink-band formation, the first bulk demonstration of tensile ductility by kinking

evidence.observation: Tensile [0001] test at RT: the flow stress starts at ~72 MPa, is serrated between ~52 and ~80 MPa, and the specimen reaches ~45% plastic strain before fracture
The tensile gauge is filled with fine bands inclined to the [0001] tensile direction, across which the marked basal-plane trace kinks

sub_claims.claim_text: Dilute LPSO nanoplates, with no perfect LPSO phase, deliver LPSO-phase-level yield stress plus tensile kink-band ductility: a route to kink-strengthened dilute Mg alloys
The wavy deformation bands are deformation kink bands: their crystal rotation angle varies continuously from ~5 to ~55 deg instead of taking the fixed ~85 deg of {10-12} twins

evidence.observation: OM of the [11-20] and [01-10] specimens: straight {10-12}/{01-12} band traces plus wavy bands whose contrast is strong on the (0001) side surface and faint on (1-100)/(-2110)
Where wavy bands form, the (1-100)/(-2110) side surface develops a step-like ridge (red arrows) while the (0001) surface stays straight, so the band shear direction is parallel to [0001]

EBSD orientation maps: lenticular bands take one uniform colour distinct from the matrix, whereas the wavy bands shade continuously with position; in the [01-10] specimen uniformly red {10-12} twins and shade-varying purple kink bands coexist

Rotation-angle histograms: the lenticular bands all sit at 80-90 deg, the wavy bands spread continuously from ~5 to ~55 deg, and the [01-10] specimen shows both populations (broad ~25 deg peak and sharp ~85 deg peak)
Bright-field TEM of the kink bands: the marked basal-plane trace bends by a large, non-constant angle at each band boundary, and many low-angle (<15 deg) boundaries coexist
SAED taken at the four marked points A-D across successive kink bands: the c-axis direction differs strongly between neighbouring bands (about 60, 180, 40 and 10 deg from horizontal)
